title: Stieger et al. 2021 — Continuous sensorimotor rhythm based brain computer interface learning in a large population
description: A large longitudinal dataset of electroencephalography (EEG) recordings from 62 healthy adults performing motor imagery tasks in a brain-computer interface (BCI) learning study. The dataset comprises over 600 hours of continuous sensorimotor rhythm-based BCI control data across up to 11 training sessions per participant, containing more than 250,000 trials of four different motor-imagery tasks (left hand, right hand, both hands, and rest). This BIDS-formatted resource is designed to support the development, evaluation, and improvement of BCI algorithms for non-invasive neural control applications.
methods_description: Participants completed 7-11 online BCI training sessions, each consisting of 450 trials across 3 tasks (left-right, up-down, 2D) with 6 runs. Each trial included a 2-second inter-trial interval, 2-second target presentation, and up to 6-second feedback control period. EEG was recorded from 62 channels at 1000 Hz sampling rate using Neuroscan SynAmps RT amplifiers with a 10-10 montage. Online control employed spatial filtering (Laplacian around C3/C4), autoregressive spectral estimation (order 16), and alpha power (12 Hz ± 1.5 Hz) for generating control signals, with cursor position updated every 40 milliseconds.
